correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all adjacency eigenvalues and multiplicities from CC^T=(q+1)I+B with the correctly derived strongly regular point graph; all distance polynomials and valencies follow from the intersection array. It derives E_theta distance entries from an exact trace identity, sums their Schur squares, and diagonalizes in the distance algebra. Symbolic identities for all five coefficients/eigenvalues and a positivity identity were independently replayed; actual symplectic GQ incidence graphs for q=2,3 corroborate every entry (7300 total). q>=2 and the q=1 thin boundary are explicitly separated. Finite checks are not relied upon as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Literature inspections locate the general projector/association-scheme methods and the underlying generalized-quadrangle adjacency parameters, but do not locate the evaluated family-wide continuous-time Cesàro spectrum, positivity classification or thin-boundary transition. A symmetric 2-design incidence calculation does not apply because GQ incidence has diameter four. General eigenmatrix methods make this an explicit-specialization result, not an independently new abstract quantum mixing theory. The residual risk of an implicit or unexamined stronger Krein-parameter result remains material and is recorded.
residual_risks: A specialized generalized-quadrangle Krein-parameter or coherent-configuration paper not located in the searches may already state or imply the same complete spectrum.
The rank positivity conclusion is computable from older general eigenmatrix formulas; the contribution is the explicit natural-class evaluation, not a new projector method.
Database coverage and queried public sources cannot establish universal uniqueness or disclose unpublished results.

value.rationale: The claim is an exact all-existing-geometries classification of the physically natural long-time transport invariant on generalized quadrangle incidence graphs, with every transition-probability distance class, complete multiplicities, and strict positivity. It distinguishes full rank on nontrivial order q>=2 from the sharp thin q=1 singular boundary, and contrasts bipartite incidence geometry with prior symmetric 2-design incidence behavior. This is a motivated geometric spectral invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice or routine check. Limitations: balanced order only, no existence theorem or instantaneous mixing result.
